about: The game launcher's files under <data>/client: profiles, accounts, the version store and the profile's servers.dat. Nobody should have to sign in again or download a version again after an update. test/contracts-files.test.mjs makes two profiles, an offline account and a server list in a scratch data root and compares the text and bytes.

layout.note: relative to the data root, / separators. Mojang's own layout under versions/, libraries/ and assets/ (objects/ and indexes/), so a store is shared by every profile.

profiles.text: util.mjs writeJson; { version: 1, profiles: { <name>: profile }, defaultAccount?: <uuid> }, profiles in creation order. A new profile's keys: mc, loader, loaderVersion, java, memory, harness, server, account, assistantAccount, serverList (only when false), createdAt. A new profile folder gets options.txt with lang:en_us.

accounts.text: util.mjs writeJson with strict owner-only protection: 0600 on POSIX, an owner-only ACL on Windows, and not written at all when that fails. { version: 1, accounts: [...] }. An offline entry is { type, name, uuid } with the uuid of an offline-mode server (md5 of OfflinePlayer:<name>, version 3); a Microsoft entry also holds its tokens and expiresAt.

serversDat.about: The profile's servers.dat (client-server-list.mjs): uncompressed NBT, an unnamed compound holding the list "servers" of compounds; SpawnLoft adds { name, ip } entries in that key order and remembers which are its own in <data>/client/run/<profile>/server-list.json, written before and after the list. The list is written to servers.dat.spawnloft.tmp, fsync-ed and renamed. Strings are Java modified UTF-8. Entries the player made are never touched.

files.text: JSON.stringify({ format: 1, files }), one line, no newline; a cache
JSON.stringify(index, null, 2), no newline, under runtime/index.lock
a stamp with no newline (the index sha1 for assets)
